Entries.Text: View, paint and check the navigation data of a loaded Dark Souls II map: the map's .ngp file, with one navmesh per MSB navmesh part, the gates where navmeshes meet, and the gate graph enemies path through. Start in the Overlay tab, which draws it in the viewport; the other tabs work on what it draws.
Map {0} has no .ngp file.
Draw the map's navmeshes over the viewport, placed by the map offset as the game places them.
A click selects the nearest gate.
Flags

Draw the navmeshes: faces coloured by their flags (or one part of them), inner and open edges, edges used by gates, gate points and the gate graph's links. The legend explains each colour; Use paints with it.

Pick faces and paint their flags: the level (which enemy sizes can use the face), the type (ground, door, ladder, rope, drop, event area, water) and the attributes (blocked, door closed). Each paint stroke is one undoable edit. Flags don't change geometry, so nothing else in the file changes.
List the map's gates (where two navmeshes share boundary edges) and the links between the gates of each navmesh, which enemies path through. Gates come from the geometry and are only shown here.
Check the .ngp against the rules the game files follow, and compare the issues with the vanilla file, so only the project's changes stand out.
Only the picked navmesh
Draw and pick only the navmesh of the picked face.
Colour Faces By
Which part of each face's flags its colour shows.
All flags
One colour per combination of level, type and attributes.
Type
One colour per face type (bits 3-6): ground, door threshold, ladder, rope, drop, event area, water and so on.
Level
One colour per level (bits 0-2): which enemy sizes can use the face.
Attributes
One colour per combination of attributes (bits 7-10): blocked, door closed, closed door passable.
Faces
The faces, filled by the colour mode above.
Inner edges
Edges between two faces of the same navmesh.
Open edges
Boundary edges that no gate uses. Enemies can't leave the navmesh there.
Gate edges
Boundary edges used by a gate, where enemies cross into another navmesh.
Gate points
Each gate's point (the middle of its first edge), as a cross.
Gate links
The gate graph: a line between each pair of gates in the same navmesh, which enemies path along.

An enemy uses a face only if the face's level is greater than the enemy's. The enemy's level is its weight type minus one (probably CHR_COMMON_PARAM weightType), so 7 lets every enemy through and lower levels keep bigger enemies out.

Ground
Ordinary ground. Every enemy the level allows can walk on it.
Door approach
Small faces next to doors, walked like ground. Inferred from the positions of the game's faces.
Door threshold
The faces under a door. The door object finds them by this type and marks them closed (attribute Door closed) or locked (Blocked). Enemies without useDoor (LOGIC_COM_PARAM) can't pass a closed door.
Ladder landing
Small faces at the ends of ladders, walked like ground. Inferred from the positions of the game's faces.
Ladder
The vertical faces of a ladder. Only enemies with useLadder (LOGIC_COM_PARAM) climb them, up or down; none can stand on them.
Rope end
Crossed but not stood on. Inferred from the positions of the game's few faces (next to rope faces).
Rope
Only enemies with useRope (LOGIC_COM_PARAM) cross these faces; none can stand on them.
Type 0x38
No game file uses it. Walked like ground.
One-way drop
A steep edge enemies jump down but never climb up.
Event area
Faces that a general location event (Navigation Mesh Change) finds within its shape by this type. Scripts block and open them with the Blocked attribute.
Type 0x50
Walked like ground. Found in Earthen Peak and Shaded Woods, possibly for poison. Its use is unknown.
Water
Walked like ground. Found in shallow water (Shrine of Amana, Doors of Pharros, Shulva). Inferred from the positions of the game's faces.
Type 0x60
No game file uses it. The game blocks it.
Type 0x68
No game file uses it. The game blocks it.
Type 0x70
No game file uses it. The game blocks it.
Type 0x78
No game file uses it. The game blocks it.
no attributes
No game test reads it, and 45 game faces have it. Its use is unknown.
Blocked

No enemy can use the face. Doors set it while locked, fog walls while active, and event scripts (AddNavimeshAttribute / DeleteNavimeshAttribute, value 2) to close and open barriers. Set it here for a barrier that starts closed.
Door closed
On a door threshold, only enemies with useDoor can pass. Door objects set and clear it as they close and open; no game file stores it.
Closed door passable
On a closed door threshold, lets every enemy through. Some doors set it when they load; no game file stores it.

Rebuild

Rebuild what follows from the geometry: the edges, half-edges, bounding box and face tree of the selected navmeshes, and the gates, gate links and IDs of the whole map. Gates between two navmeshes that aren't rebuilt are kept as they are.
Rebuild Picked Navmesh
Rebuild the picked face's navmesh and its gates with neighbouring navmeshes. One undoable edit.
Rebuild All

Rebuild every navmesh and every gate. The face trees differ from the game's (valid, but built by a different rule), and 144 vanilla navmeshes whose edges the game's tool welded get plain edge tables. One undoable edit.
The rebuild produces the same file, so there is nothing to change.

Move navmesh vertices with a brush (Raise, Lower, Drag, Smooth). Edits show in the overlay until committed. Committing rebuilds the moved navmeshes' bounding boxes and face trees, and the map's gates, as one undoable edit. Keep Linked on near gates: an edge that moves away from its neighbour's edge loses its gate.
Write the moved vertices into the .ngp, and rebuild the moved navmeshes' bounding boxes and face trees and the map's gates, links and IDs. One undoable edit.
Also move other navmeshes' vertices under the brush, with the same falloff, so edges shared by two navmeshes (their gates) stay joined.

Committed {1} moved vertices in {0} navmeshes, but gates went from {2} to {3}: an edge moved away from its neighbour's, so enemies can no longer cross there. Undo, or move both sides (Linked) back together.

List the map's navmeshes: each MSB navmesh part and the .ngp mesh at the same position. Generate creates a navmesh (or replaces the selected one) from the selected collision parts; Duplicate copies one, moved by an offset; Remove deletes one with its part. Ladder adds a ladder at the selected ladder objects; Drop adds a one-way drop from the ledge nearest the picked point to the floor below. Gates, links and IDs are updated. Each is one undoable edit.

Ladder

Add a ladder at each selected ladder object, built like the game's own ladders: a column of vertical Ladder faces 0.70 m wide at the object's position, facing its +Z, with a 0.70 m square Ladder landing at each end. The bottom landing is behind the object on the floor at its foot; the top landing is in front of it on the floor near the top of its bounds. Both are cut into those floors so enemies can step on and off. The ladder goes into the bottom floor's navmesh; a top floor in another navmesh meets the ladder through a gate.

Drop

Add a one-way drop from a ledge to the floor below, built like the game's own drops: steep faces joining the ledge's open edge to the floor beneath, so enemies jump down but don't climb up. The ledge is the picked navmesh's open edge nearest the picked point. The floor is found below the ledge, at a wall's foot or further out from it, and the drop's bottom is cut into it.

Highest

Regenerate the whole map's navigation from its collision parts (DS2: Scholar of the First Sin's collision) as one undoable edit. Faces that paths can reach from the seeds are split into the map's navmeshes, one per MSB navmesh part, so the MSB stays the same; gates are found again where navmeshes meet. Flags are carried over from the faces under them, steep faces become one-way drops, and ladders are rebuilt at the ladder objects. Door thresholds aren't created: paint them with Paint Under Selection in the Flags tab.
Regenerate

One generation over every collision part of the map, pruned to what the seeds reach and split into the map's navmeshes. The navmesh parts and their order stay the same; each navmesh's faces are replaced.
Seed from the current navmeshes

Keep the generated faces that paths can reach from the current navmeshes' faces, as well as from the map's generators and start points. When off, only the generators and start points are seeds, which may leave out areas where no enemy stands.
Seed from new and selected collision

Keep the generated faces over collision you added (collision files the game's own binder doesn't have, or created or changed this session) and over the selected collision parts, with everything they reach. A new area isn't joined to the current navmesh, so without this it would be left out. Faces there with no navmesh under them go to the navmesh named by their collision part's NvmGroup, or else the nearest one.
Regenerate seeds from these new or selected collision parts: {0}
Keep the navmesh split

Put each new face in the navmesh of the current face under it, so the map keeps its own split. Elsewhere, and when off, the collision under the face decides: the navmesh whose NavmeshGroup bit its collision part shares in its NvmGroups. Faces with neither join a neighbouring navmesh.
Keep face flags

Give each new face the level and area type (ground, event area, water…) that most of the current faces under it have. The small strip types (doors, ladders, landings, ropes, drops) aren't carried over: ladders and drops are rebuilt below, and you can paint door thresholds. When off, every face is level 7 ground.
Mark steep faces as drops
Set ground faces at least this steep to One-way drop, like the game's drops (median 65°).
Make ladders at the ladder objects
After regenerating, add a ladder at every ladder object (oXX_09XX) in the map, like Models → Ladder.
